clue.text: What records are for sport champion?

parts.note: to sport is to play, as children do
to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking what a sports champion's records are for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' and 'champion' look like nouns but both work as verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Recordings exist so they can be replayed later; replaying them is their whole purpose.

clue.text: Beginning to drive one expands torso muscles? Legs, more like

definitions.text: Beginning to drive one expands torso muscles? Legs, more like

indicators.note: the muscles are pushed apart by the letters placed within them

parts.note: pecs and abs are muscles of the chest and stomach; one of each is used

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word drive is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
pecs and abs are muscles of the chest and stomach; one of each is used

explanation.surface: Does pedalling a passenger build chest and stomach muscles? No, the legs get the workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expands' means the torso muscles are pushed apart by the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered rickshaw taxi is driven by the rider's legs, as the clue jokes.

clue.text: A person patrolling a depleted area, one like a rainforest

indicators.note: patrolling an area means going all round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a man is a person
taken as written

indicators.note: depleted means emptied out, so the word for area loses its last letter

parts.note: a zone is an area
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ranger patrols a deforested area that was once rainforest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' means the word for area loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon basin holds the world's largest tropical rainforest, so jungle-like terrain is described thus.

clue.text: All-inclusive form's place to fill in limits of employment

parts.note: a blank is a space on a form to be filled in

indicators.note: only the edge letters of the word employment are used

explanation.surface: A job application form with a space for the dates of employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket ban or policy covers everything without exception.

clue.text: Relish smoker, making him a little shelter

indicators.note: making the second word into the third swaps one set of letters for another

parts.note: a chimney smokes, so it is a smoker
taken as written
a hut is a small shelter

explanation.surface: A smoker is banished to a tiny shelter outside.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy condiment of fruit and vinegar is a relish served with food.

clue.text: Middle-distance runner lapping a person at the post?

indicators.note: lapping a runner means going round them, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a miler races over the mile, a middle distance

explanation.surface: A miler overtakes someone a whole lap ahead as they near the finishing post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' here is the mail, not the finishing post of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sends things by post is one who mails them, a sender of letters.

clue.text: Required minutes with a right-winger

parts.note: and means with, together
a Tory is a British Conservative, of the political right

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician is obliged to keep the meeting minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compulsory is required by rule, with no choice allowed.

clue.text: Two for one, say, splitting place in tomb

indicators.note: splitting a word apart lets another piece sit inside it

parts.note: to inter is to bury, placing in a tomb
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Two bodies share one burial place in a split tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two for one' is not a shop offer: it reads 'two, for instance', and two is an example of a whole number.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole numbers such as two are examples of this kind of number.

clue.text: Trade ban consequently restricts a degree of commerce

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, consequently
the MBA, Master of Business Administration, is a business degree

explanation.surface: A trade ban therefore limits how much commerce happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A government order forbidding commerce with a country is a ban on trading.

clue.text: Defaced Qur'an made European individual prone to overreacting

indicators.note: something defaced is spoilt and disfigured, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the holy book's name, letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vandalised a holy book and made a European overreact.
explanation.walkthrough: E, for European, joins QURAN and MADE in the letters that 'Defaced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who makes a theatrical fuss over small things.

clue.text: Billions invested in weekday train network

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Tue is the short form of Tuesday
B is the usual abbreviation for billion(s)

explanation.surface: Billions of pounds are poured into a rail network on a weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground is popularly called the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: London's underground railway system is known as the Tube.

clue.text: Undercover alias, name to tack on when turning into an obstructor

indicators.note: going into something means being put inside it, so the following pieces sit within another

parts.note: something that clogs a pipe is a clogger
AKA, 'also known as', introduces an alias

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading the word add backwards

parts.note: to tack something on is to add it

explanation.surface: An undercover agent's alias, with a name tacked on, turns them into a hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when turning' makes DDA from ADD; AKA, N and DDA then go into CLOGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes secret spy work, the stuff of espionage thrillers, so it means covert.

clue.text: Cheerfully losing heart to son in need of a shave

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are lost and replaced by another piece

parts.note: doing something brightly means doing it cheerfully
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cheerful man loses heart because his son badly needs a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart to' swaps GH, the middle two letters of BRIGHTLY, for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubble on an unshaven chin feels rough and spiky, like stiff hairs.

clue.text: Being easily influenced without power is a hindrance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: pliability is the quality of being easily bent or swayed
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Being a pushover without any power holds you back.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or drawback that holds someone back, a handicap, is described by this word.

clue.text: It's a deal that no longer involves collapse of euro

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something up inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: yon is an archaic word for that, no longer in use

indicators.note: a collapse knocks a word's letters out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A financial deal that no longer depends on the euro collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that no longer' signals an archaic word, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in agreement to a bet or proposal, the phrase accepts the deal.

clue.text: Ring, once forged, ending in Doom on mountain route

indicators.note: something forged is hammered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word Doom is taken

parts.note: a pass is a route through mountains

explanation.surface: Tolkien's Ring, once forged, ends in Mount Doom.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Lord of the Rings the Ring is forged and destroyed in Mount Doom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it, a verb meaning circle or encircle.

clue.text: Clear a path in criminal group's characteristic manner?

parts.note: a gang is a criminal group
someone's way is their characteristic manner

explanation.surface: A gang clears a route in its own typical fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouted as an exclamation, the word tells people to stand aside and make way.

clue.text: Settle on Scottish island, secure after docking

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: docking means cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to secure something is to get it

explanation.surface: Settling on a Scottish island after the ferry docks safely.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle an affair is to organise or sort it out.

clue.text: Nought's destroyed in bit of fire

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: the word nought plus the S of its 's, read as written

explanation.surface: A zero is destroyed by a piece of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A single discharge of a firearm is one shot, a small part of gunfire.

clue.text: Hard-boiled egg's first dropped in clean, icy liquid

indicators.note: a liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters are rearranged
dropped means let fall out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word egg is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard-boiled egg is dropped into clean, icy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg's first dropped' takes E out of CLEAN to give CLAN; 'liquid' then rearranges CLAN plus ICY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-boiled person is tough and unsentimental, expecting the worst of people.

clue.text: Mad tea party guest after companion's cup

indicators.note: after means following, so the guest's name comes second

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour, abbreviates companion
Alice attends the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's story

explanation.surface: Alice at the Mad Hatter's tea party grabs her companion's cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet or ceremonial drinking vessel, especially the communion one, is a kind of cup.

clue.text: Changing tack initially, vague about certain WMDs

indicators.note: changing tack at the start swaps the order of the opening letters

parts.note: something vague is unclear

explanation.surface: A vague dossier on weapons of mass destruction changes its line.
explanation.walkthrough: The U is moved one place, so the first two letters trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic weapons are a kind of weapon of mass destruction, so the adjective concerns them.

clue.text: Oil source is hollow stone with wrinkly covering

indicators.note: a covering wraps round what it covers

parts.note: a wrinkled face is lined

indicators.note: hollowed out, the word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A wrinkled stone shell hides a hollow centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is just a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seeds are pressed to make linseed oil, so the seed is an oil source.

clue.text: I'm multitalented, recalling title about Parnassian Queen but forgetting paragraph

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a name is a title
C, circa, means about

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, relating to Parnassus, the mountain of the Muses
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A versatile poet recalls a title about a Queen of Parnassus, leaving out a paragraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting paragraph' takes PAR from PARNASSIAN to leave NASSIAN; NAME, C, NASSIAN and ER together are then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted across many fields, art and science alike, is called this, after Leonardo-style polymaths.

clue.text: Some rain favoured Castlereagh's outer parts

parts.note: something in favour is in

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of the name are used

explanation.surface: Castlereagh, the statesman or the Northern Irish place, has rain on its fringes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is measured in this unit, so a small amount of rain is one.

clue.text: I sound similar at first, ignoring a non-reader

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out

parts.note: words alliterate when their opening sounds match
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot read hears only that the words start alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A person unable to read or write is unlettered, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Holy person has actual clothing here

definitions.text: Holy person has actual clothing here

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: the very thing is the actual one
ST, saint, is a holy person

explanation.surface: A saint keeps real vestments in this church room.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the room, where clergy robes are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: This church room is where priests store their vestments and change into them.

clue.text: Someone wishing to keep piano turns performed again

indicators.note: turns means the result is read backwards
keeping something is holding it inside

parts.note: one who desires is a desirer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a piano turns up to perform once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts P inside DESIRER; 'turns' then reads the lot from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeat performance, so a reprised role was played again.
